oval-intro: The LC series oval gear flowmeter is a classic positive displacement meter for liquids that fill a pipe under pressure. It is simple in structure, reliable and accurate, needs no special inlet or outlet flow conditions, and covers a wide range of viscosities and flow rates. It is especially suited to metering fuels and oils.
oval-principle: Driven by the pressure difference between inlet and outlet (P₁ > P₂), a pair of meshing oval gears A and B turn alternately. (a) Gear A is turned by the pressure difference and drives gear B, while liquid is held in the crescent-shaped space beneath A. (b) Both gears rotate and carry this liquid towards the outlet. (c) A new crescent-shaped space forms above gear B. Each revolution discharges four crescent volumes, so counting the gear revolutions gives the volume of liquid that has passed.
oval-caption: Oval gear working principle: stages (a)–(c) of the gear rotation

helical-intro: The helical dual rotor flowmeter is a new-generation positive displacement meter of distinctive design, precision-machined and assembled. A pair of helical rotors moves inside the measuring chamber, dividing, measuring, carrying and discharging the liquid. Timing gears keep the two rotors from touching as they turn, so the meter runs smoothly and quietly with little wear and high accuracy. It handles a wide range of viscosities and lets fine particles pass without jamming. It is widely used for custody-transfer metering and process control in petrochemicals, metallurgy, electronics and port terminals.
helical-principle: Flow is measured inside the measuring chamber. Under the pressure of the liquid, the pair of helical rotors turns; the closed spaces formed between the rotors and the chamber wall (shaded in the drawing) discharge eight times their volume per revolution. Counting the rotor revolutions therefore gives the total volume, and the revolutions per second give the instantaneous flow rate. The rotors turn at constant speed, so the flow is even and almost pulsation-free.

miniature-intro: The LC-W series miniature flowmeter is a positive displacement meter for very small flows, developed by building on advanced foreign technology. It offers low flow capability, simple construction, high accuracy, easy use and long service life. It adapts well to different viscosities, places no special demands on flow pattern or pressure, and can meter liquid flowing under gravity. The display shows total, batch and instantaneous flow with a reset function, and supports both local display and remote transmission.
miniature-principle: The LC-W miniature flowmeter works on the oval gear positive displacement principle. Driven by the pressure difference between inlet and outlet (P₁ > P₂), a pair of oval gears A and B turns alternately, and each revolution discharges a fixed volume of liquid. The sensor detects the gear rotation through the housing, without touching the liquid and without any mechanical transmission.

roots-intro: The roots (lobed impeller) flowmeter is a type of positive displacement meter for gasoline, kerosene, diesel and other refined oils, and can transmit the flow to a secondary instrument via a pulse transmitter. Its design is modern, well proportioned and practical: light, accurate and easy to install and use. It is widely used for oil metering in petrochemicals, power, metallurgy, transport, defence and commerce.
roots-principle: When liquid flows through the measuring chamber, a pressure difference forms between inlet and outlet and turns the lobed impellers. A pair of drive gears fixed on the impeller shafts keeps the two impellers turning together. The chamber volume consists of two crescent-shaped spaces, the unit volume. Each revolution delivers four unit volumes, so the number of revolutions is proportional to the flow; a reduction gear drives the counter and pointer to display the volume that has passed.

rn-1: Clean the pipeline thoroughly before installation and fit a filter upstream of the meter; if the liquid contains gas, fit an air separator or degassing filter.
rn-2: Install with the impeller shafts horizontal, i.e. the dial vertical; fit the control and shut-off valves at the inlet and outlet.
rn-3: The arrow on the meter body must point in the direction of flow.
rn-4: On continuous process lines, fit a bypass valve on the horizontal run for regular cleaning and service; on vertical pipes, install the meter in a bypass so debris cannot fall into it.
rn-5: For easier reading, the counter can be rotated 90° or 180° once the meter is correctly installed.
turbine-intro: The LWGY series turbine flow sensor works on the torque-balance principle and is a velocity-type flowmeter. It is simple, light, accurate, repeatable and responsive, and easy to install, maintain and use. It is widely used in petroleum, chemicals, metallurgy, water supply and paper-making. Used with a display instrument, it measures liquids in closed pipes that do not corrode 1Cr18Ni9Ti or 2Cr13 stainless steel, corundum (Al₂O₃) or hard alloy and are free of fibres and particles; with suitable instruments it can also perform batch control and over-limit alarms. The explosion-proof version (Ex d IIB T6) can be used in hazardous areas.
turbine-principle: As the liquid flows through the sensor body, the impeller blades, set at an angle to the flow, receive a driving torque. Once this overcomes friction and fluid resistance, the impeller turns and settles at a steady speed proportional to the flow velocity. The magnetically permeable blades pass through the field of the pickup (a permanent magnet and coil), periodically changing the magnetic flux and inducing electrical pulses in the coil. These are amplified and shaped into a continuous rectangular pulse train sent to the display instrument. Within the rated range the pulse frequency f is proportional to the flow rate Q: Q = 3600 × f / K, where K is the meter factor given on the calibration certificate.

tn-1: Install where the pipe is free from vibration, strong electromagnetic interference and heat radiation, with easy access for maintenance; outdoors, protect the sensor from direct sun and rain.
tn-2: Turbine meters are sensitive to distorted velocity profiles and swirl. Provide the straight pipe lengths in the table; if the upstream fittings are unknown, use at least 20D upstream and 5D downstream, or fit a flow conditioner.
tn-3: Horizontal installation: pipe tilt within 5°. Vertical installation: deviation within 5°, and the flow must be upward.
tn-4: Where flow cannot be stopped, fit a bypass with reliable shut-off valves. On new pipework, flush the line with a spool piece in place of the sensor before installing it.
tn-5: Fit a filter upstream if the liquid contains impurities and an air eliminator if it contains gas; the flow control valve goes downstream of the sensor; add a check valve where reverse flow may occur.
tn-6: Keep the sensor concentric with the pipe and do not let gaskets protrude into the bore; do not install at the highest point of a horizontal line; insulate the sensor and adjacent pipe for liquids that solidify easily.
